what_happened: Reconstructed the exact end-to-end mechanism for task #467's historical scope-excursion drop by matching the issue's zero-phase/zero-dispatch-seq shape and exact timestamp against git-commit-scoped.sh's own internal V10 issue-record call (not WORK(h)/(i) or git-commit-phase.sh's self-check, which have distinct message text) and against the task-creation commit's timestamp, establishing that no staging-side fix is needed -- only the Containment allowlist itself is defective.

Research report pinned exact edit points (git-commit-scoped.sh:499, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:1670, git-commit-phase.sh's absent Site 2 allowlist) and settled both the consolidation verdict and the membership list, so planning only had to verify them by direct read rather than re-derive; all three were confirmed accurate. Plan validated with 0 warnings on first pass.

Research recommended sourcing the shared library at all three sites but did not specify the source-failure fallback. A defensive 'source ... 2>/dev/null' that silently yields nothing would EMPTY the splice and regress today's admission of specs/TODO.md and specs/state.json at Sites 1 and 3 -- a narrower scope than before the fix. Plan adds Decision 2: fall back to the hardcoded two-literal pair on any source/function failure, pinned by a Site 3 fixture (Z18).

test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh has 25 pre-existing [FAIL] assertions (acceptance/fixture/regression/skeleton-followup/case-9xx status-transition blocks, plus one carve-out assertion expecting specs/state.json in a commit) unrelated to task 469's engine-written-state allowlist change. Confirmed by running a byte-for-byte pre-edit copy of both orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh and its test suite (git show HEAD: versions) in isolation: identical 25 failures, identical 'cleanup: command not found' trap error, 271 passed vs 278 passed post-edit (the +7 delta is exactly this phase's own new events.jsonl-admission assertions, all passing). run-all.sh classifies the suite as a NEW failure (not in known-failures.txt), which will surface again at Phase 6's full-battery gate; out of scope for task 469 to fix.

Phase 5 required registering Phase 1's two new files in agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json's provides.scripts (via sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write, 2 entries) and correcting git-staging-scope.md's line_count in index-entries.json (via the deployed generate-context-line-counts.sh --write) so gate 3 (doc-lint) reflects only expected pre-redeploy drift. Both files are outside task 469's declared file_scope, and index-entries.json's working-tree diff is entangled with unrelated line_count corrections for other extensions' content already dirty from concurrent sibling tasks before this phase touched it. Both fixes were made on disk (safe: deploy-headless.sh reads the working tree directly) but deliberately left OUT of this task's own scoped commits to avoid sweeping sibling tasks' unrelated deltas into task 469's commit history. Recorded so the omission is legible to whoever closes out this batch.

Phase 6's real-commit observation: specs/events.jsonl carries a genuine 2462-line uncommitted delta spanning 111 distinct task numbers at observation time (confirmed via git diff HEAD -- specs/events.jsonl), heavily interleaved with concurrent sibling tasks' own event rows -- this is the expected, known consequence of committing a shared append-only store that the plan itself anticipated, not a defect. The delta is genuinely not synthesized: it accumulated from real concurrent /orchestrate activity across this session.
